description.value: The study investigated behavioral and neural correlates of emotional reactivity and cognitive regulation in adults with social anxiety disorder and healthy controls during social and physical threat.

spans.text: This study investigated behavioral and neural correlates of emotional reactivity and cognitive regulation in patients and controls during processing of social and physical threat stimuli.

spans.text: We expected to find (1) no difference in SAD and HC for emotional reactivity and regulation for physical threat, (2) greater reactivity to harsh faces in SAD than HC, and (3) deficits in regulation in SAD versus HC for social threat stimuli.

Participants were trained to implement cognitive-linguistic regulation of emotional reactivity induced by social (harsh facial expressions) and physical (violent scenes) threat while undergoing functional magnetic resonance imaging and providing behavioral ratings of negative emotion experience.

description.value: Participants viewed social and physical threat stimuli and either looked at them or regulated their emotional reactions using cognitive-linguistic reappraisal.

Behavioral responses were made using a custom button box and recorded using Eprime software.
Each 12s trial consisted of an instruction (Look or Regulate) (3s), stimulus (6s), and emotion rating (3s).

stimuli.value: Harsh facial expressions, violent scenes, and neutral scenes.

spans.text: There were 25 trials for each of five conditions: Look Harsh Face, Regulate Harsh Face, Look Violent Scene, Regulate Violent Scene, and Look Neutral Scene.
Behavioral responses were made using a custom button box and recorded using Eprime software.
Look Harsh Face
There were 25 trials for each of five conditions: Look Harsh Face, Regulate Harsh Face, Look Violent Scene, Regulate Violent Scene, and Look Neutral Scene.

description.value: Participants viewed color photographs of actors displaying harsh expressions combining anger and contempt for 6 seconds after a 3-second Look instruction, then rated their negative emotion for 3 seconds; they were instructed to just look without trying to control or modulate emotional reactivity.

spans.text: Each 12s trial consisted of an instruction (Look or Regulate) (3s), stimulus (6s), and emotion rating (3s).
Regulate Harsh Face
There were 25 trials for each of five conditions: Look Harsh Face, Regulate Harsh Face, Look Violent Scene, Regulate Violent Scene, and Look Neutral Scene.

description.value: Participants viewed color photographs of actors displaying harsh expressions combining anger and contempt for 6 seconds after a 3-second Regulate instruction, using cognitive-linguistic reinterpretation strategies such as “This does not involve me,” “This does not influence me,” or “This does not impact me” to reduce negative reactions, then rated their negative emotion for 3 seconds.

spans.text: Specifically, they were instructed to re-interpret the content of the picture using cognitive-linguistic strategies including “This does not involve me,” “This does not influence me,” or “This does not impact me” for harsh faces
Look Violent Scene
There were 25 trials for each of five conditions: Look Harsh Face, Regulate Harsh Face, Look Violent Scene, Regulate Violent Scene, and Look Neutral Scene.

description.value: Participants viewed color photographs depicting a person being violently attacked for 6 seconds after a 3-second Look instruction, then rated their negative emotion for 3 seconds; they were instructed to just look without trying to control or modulate emotional reactivity.

spans.text: Regulate Violent Scene
There were 25 trials for each of five conditions: Look Harsh Face, Regulate Harsh Face, Look Violent Scene, Regulate Violent Scene, and Look Neutral Scene.

description.value: Participants viewed color photographs depicting a person being violently attacked for 6 seconds after a 3-second Regulate instruction, using cognitive-linguistic reinterpretation strategies such as “The person will be okay” or “The person was not really hurt” to reduce negative reactions, then rated their negative emotion for 3 seconds.

spans.text: “The person will be okay,” “The person was not really hurt,” and so forth for the violent scenes.
Look Neutral Scene
There were 25 trials for each of five conditions: Look Harsh Face, Regulate Harsh Face, Look Violent Scene, Regulate Violent Scene, and Look Neutral Scene.

description.value: Participants viewed non-arousing, non-social color photographs of mundane scenes such as pavement, a garage door, or wood siding for 6 seconds after a 3-second Look instruction, then rated their negative emotion for 3 seconds; they were instructed to just look without attempting regulation.

spans.text: Neutral scenes, used as the baseline comparison for both social and physical threat, consisted of non-arousing, non-social color photos of mundane scenes (e.g., pavement, garage door, wood siding).
